target.scope_decision: Only native x86_64 ELF workloads and the x86_64 syscall ABI are in scope for this manifest.

x32_abi.rationale: A-PRE-0 qualifies the declared native x86_64 runtime, not alternate x86 ABIs.
x32_abi.qualification_requirement: The launcher boundary must reject x32 workloads or the ABI must be added as a separately versioned manifest before qualification.

i386_compat_abi.rationale: A-PRE-0 qualifies the declared native x86_64 runtime, not 32-bit compatibility workloads.
i386_compat_abi.qualification_requirement: The launcher boundary must reject i386 compat workloads or the ABI must be added as a separately versioned manifest before qualification.

target.version_gated_syscalls: Use the locally hashed table from the official linux 7.0.0-34.34 source package matched to the fresh fadena-lab package identity. Its SHA-256 matches the preserved 385-row register table; the prior Noble/HWE acquisition remains auxiliary. Absence from the bound table is not silently treated as coverage.

freeze_blockers: All 385 native table rows are explicitly enumerated but remain UNKNOWN: none has a final surface assignment or effect-based exclusion.
Per-surface argument prose has not yet been expanded into finite selector/value partitions required by coverage_unit_contract.
A static call-site mapping from the targeted workload snapshot through Python/native/dependency layers to these surfaces is not complete.
qualification_open_items_not_freeze_bloc: Launcher enforcement rejecting the explicitly out-of-scope x32/i386 compatibility ABIs is not qualified.
Default-deny for opaque APIs is a proposed policy, not demonstrated active enforcement.
Surface statuses and sensor/control evidence still contain UNKNOWN or are not independently qualified.

rules: A syscall name is not by itself a complete coverage unit when arguments select different operations, resources, namespaces, or kernel objects.
Split a unit when a flag, command, address family, ancillary-data type, resource class, or phase changes the security meaning or the enforceability of observation/blocking.
Keep one canonical syscall definition; represent its participation in other semantics through relations and alternate_paths rather than duplicate coverage claims.
The finite set of argument partitions must be explicit. Values outside an admitted partition are UNKNOWN unless an active, verified control denies them.
A missing or unavailable syscall on the bound kernel table is recorded as NOT_APPLICABLE only when the exact table identity proves absence; otherwise it remains unresolved.
Per-unit qualification state is independent of inventory freeze. Freezing scope does not upgrade UNKNOWN.
Selectors include syscall-specific scalar flags/commands and semantic object classes; no unit may be keyed only by syscall name when the same call reaches different resources or operations.

Where seccomp cannot inspect pointer-referenced data or bind a numeric FD to an object type, do not claim an argument-specific default-deny allowlist as enforceable; deny the whole syscall or use a separately qualified control.
coverage_unit_contract.completion_note: Current surface argument lists identify partition axes but do not enumerate every finite selector/value partition. This is a freeze blocker, not permission to treat all values as one covered unit.

syscall_disposition_contract.universe: Every common or 64 syscall entry in arch/x86/entry/syscalls/syscall_64.tbl from the official Ubuntu linux 7.0.0-34.34 source package, bound to the read-only fadena-lab identity acquisition by installed package/version and table SHA-256.
required_disposition: assigned to one or more canonical surface IDs, with canonical definition and explicit cross-surface relations; or
excluded with a threat-model rationale and an explicit statement of which effect classes it cannot reach.
syscall_disposition_contract.unlisted_or_new_syscall_rule: A syscall added by a kernel/table update or encountered without a disposition invalidates the manifest identity and is UNKNOWN until a versioned static review updates it.
syscall_disposition_contract.unknown_handling: Every common/64 row has an explicit static_disposition_review. Historical OBSERVED/BLOCKED case outcomes are recorded only for exact named subcases and do not promote syscall-wide disposition. Human-adjudicated candidate memberships are limited to the explicit relation and do not establish effects, reachability, coverage, or readiness; unclosed variants/routes remain UNKNOWN.

historical_case_adjudication_summary.authority: Existing evidence only; no new probe, TALOS execution, suite, parser, or A-PRE validator run in this update.
historical_case_adjudication_summary.rule: A case outcome OBSERVED/BLOCKED is not a syscall-row disposition. A row remains UNKNOWN while any relevant argument partition, route, resource, phase, or threat-model question remains open.

documentary_review_summary.rule: A documented axis or historical example is not a finite partition. Values/combinations not explicitly bounded remain UNKNOWN.

variant_closure_rule: An item above is resolved only by finite selector/value partitions with explicit admitted/excluded values, resource class, phase, alternate paths, and closure criterion. If a kernel control cannot inspect a selector (for example pointer-referenced data or an FD's object type), the entire syscall must be denied or another separately qualified control must cover it; no argument-specific enforcement is inferred.

change_control.rule: Once frozen, any kernel ABI/table, runtime, workload snapshot, surface list, argument partition, relation, exclusion, or policy change requires a new manifest version and explicit re-review. New mechanisms are never added silently during qualification.
change_control.unknown_policy: Freeze describes scope only; it does not upgrade any surface or case from UNKNOWN.

surfaces.name: Filesystem path discovery and open/create
arguments_and_variants: absolute and relative pathname
dirfd identity and resolution
creation and resolution flags
symlink and mount-boundary resolution
result and resolved resource identity
surfaces.resource: Filesystem objects reachable by pathname, dirfd, or directory enumeration.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: A potentially hostile workload must not obtain undeclared filesystem resources by pathname or metadata/discovery operations.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Enumerate each applicable call and relevant argument class; demonstrate attributable allowed operations or policy-correlated denial for prohibited resources; unresolved path/dirfd/resource remains UNKNOWN.
surfaces.human_adjudicated_membership_scope: Human-adjudicated S01 candidate memberships are limited to the filesystem-object resolution, selection, identification, interaction, or location-discovery dimension stated per row; they do not assign the syscall's complete functional effect, prove reachability, or change its UNKNOWN disposition.

surfaces.name: Data transfer through descriptors
arguments_and_variants: source and destination descriptor identity
requested count versus completed return count
offsets, vector count, flags, and partial transfers
resource class and whether payload is intentionally omitted
surfaces.resource: Bytes transferred through regular, anonymous, pipe, or socket descriptors.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: Descriptor I/O can read or mutate resources independently of pathname visibility.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Attribute both endpoint objects and the actual result for each call family; do not infer payload or completed bytes from requested lengths.

surfaces.name: Descriptor lifecycle, inheritance, and acquisition
arguments_and_variants: fcntl S03 scope is restricted to commands F_DUPFD, F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, F_GETFD, and F_SETFD; all other commands are outside this adjudication.
FD_CLOEXEC state and descriptor survival/purge across successful execve/execveat transitions; executable image replacement remains the separate S11/Processes dimension.
execveat executable resolution/selection via dirfd or executable FD as applicable is distinct from inheritance of other descriptors; dirfd resolution crosses S01.
close_range effects must distinguish descriptor closure, CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC, and CLOSE_RANGE_UNSHARE.
descriptor allowlist at sandbox entry.
descriptor identity before/after duplication or acquisition; pidfd_getfd local acquisition crosses IPC/Processes and S09.
surfaces.resource: Open file descriptions, sockets, and other kernel object capabilities held by a process.
exclusions: Deliberate capability injection by trusted infrastructure is not an in-scope adversary action; injected descriptors remain useful as sensor-sensitivity controls.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: The trusted launcher must pass only declared descriptors and prevent undeclared capabilities from entering the workload at the sandbox boundary.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Qualify launcher FD hygiene at entry and enumerate later acquisition/duplication/exec transitions; controls must identify the permitted FD set and fail closed on unknown descriptors.

human_adjudicated_membership_batch.scope_rule: Only the per-syscall S03 dimensions recorded in the human_adjudication fields are accepted. Other commands, variants, surfaces, syscall-wide disposition, reachability, and control outcomes remain unadjudicated.

surfaces.name: Filesystem namespace and metadata mutation
arguments_and_variants: source/destination path and dirfd
FD-targeted versus pathname-targeted mutation
mount, symlink, and race-sensitive resolution
operation-specific flags and result
surfaces.resource: Filesystem names, object contents, metadata, and node creation/removal.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: A potentially hostile workload may alter protected filesystem state by name or through an already-open descriptor.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Freeze operation/variant inventory and attribute affected object(s), or correlate denials to active policy and protected resource; ambiguous resolution remains UNKNOWN.

surfaces.name: File-backed memory mappings
arguments_and_variants: backing FD/object identity
MAP_SHARED versus MAP_PRIVATE
protection, offset, length, remap, and sync flags
mapping lifecycle and independently verified resulting content
surfaces.resource: File-backed mappings, including mappings of resources outside the visible pathname namespace.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: A file-backed mapping can retain access to an object through an FD and shared stores can persist outside the process.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Distinguish mapping creation from memory loads/stores; attribute backing object and independently establish relevant effects or demonstrate the resource cannot enter.

surfaces.name: Anonymous mappings and memfd objects
arguments_and_variants: MAP_ANONYMOUS and MAP_SHARED/MAP_PRIVATE combinations
memfd flags and seals via fcntl
process sharing, FD transfer, mapping consumers, and content lifetime
surfaces.resource: Private anonymous memory and descriptor-backed anonymous objects, including memfd.
exclusions: Private anonymous memory confined to one process is not itself an external effect; cross-process sharing and descriptor transfer are not excluded.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: Anonymous objects avoid pathname controls and may become shared capabilities through FD inheritance or IPC.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Separate private process memory from shared anonymous/memfd objects; account for creation, transfer, consumers, and any externally visible effect.

surfaces.name: IP network communication
arguments_and_variants: AF_INET and AF_INET6 endpoints
socket type/protocol, destination, peer, and return result
TCP/UDP and socket-option variants
connected socket inherited at sandbox entry
Only AF_INET and AF_INET6 are admitted by this proposed scope; all other socket domains are default-deny unless assigned to S08 or added by a versioned manifest change.
exclusions: Other address families are outside the admitted set and proposed default-deny; enforcement is not yet qualified.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: Network communication may expose data or access undeclared external resources.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Attribute endpoint/peer and transfer result, or demonstrate an active network boundary blocks the specific prohibited attempt; namespace existence alone is insufficient.

surfaces.name: AF_UNIX endpoint and local socket communication
arguments_and_variants: AF_UNIX stream/datagram/seqpacket
pathname and abstract namespace addresses
local peer identity and transfer result
preconnected socket descriptor
surfaces.resource: Local Unix-domain socket endpoints and peers.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: AF_UNIX is independent of the IP network namespace and can communicate with local or preconnected peers.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Identify endpoint/peer and operation, or establish a specific boundary prevents the prohibited peer connection; a missing pathname does not rule out a preconnected FD.

surfaces.name: Capability transfer through sockets
arguments_and_variants: SCM_RIGHTS control messages and received descriptor identities
SCM_CREDENTIALS treated as peer-identity metadata, not as FD transfer
object identity and subsequent use of each received FD
surfaces.resource: Transfer of authority over files, sockets, memfd, or other kernel objects between processes.
exclusions: SCM_CREDENTIALS is not itself a capability-transfer mechanism; peer identity may still be a required attribution field.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: Descriptor passing can introduce a new resource capability after sandbox entry without pathname resolution.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Enumerate supported ancillary-message operations and correlate sender, receiver, transferred object, and later use, or demonstrate that the transfer path is blocked.

surfaces.name: Classic IPC, shared-memory IPC, and process coordination
arguments_and_variants: distinguish data transport, shared-memory object, synchronization, and signaling
identify peer/process and object where applicable
associate futex operations with the shared memory region they coordinate
surfaces.resource: Pipes, event counters, SysV IPC objects, shared-memory regions, and process signal state.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: These mechanisms can transfer data, share memory, or coordinate actions outside pathname and IP-network controls.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Classify transport versus synchronization, identify relevant endpoints/objects, and account for shared-memory and descriptor-transfer edges.

surfaces.name: Process tree, exec, wait, and termination
arguments_and_variants: clone flags and child/parent relationships
successful exec transitions
tracee identity, per-process trace closure, and terminal status
surfaces.resource: Execution branches and descendants capable of exercising any other workload surface.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: A potentially hostile workload may delegate effects to descendants or exploit missing process coverage.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Prove every descendant is followed through exec and termination, with complete per-process evidence; process capture alone does not close descendant effect surfaces.

surfaces.name: io_uring
arguments_and_variants: native x86_64 and any ABI variants admitted by the target policy
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: Ring operations can perform I/O through shared submission/completion memory not fully described by ordinary read/write trace events.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Every listed syscall is denied by a verified active policy or ring operations are observed with sufficient request/completion attribution.

surfaces.name: Linux native AIO
arguments_and_variants: native x86_64 and any ABI variants admitted by the target policy
surfaces.resource: Linux kernel native asynchronous I/O contexts and requests.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: Asynchronous requests can separate submission, worker execution, and completion from ordinary synchronous operation attribution.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Every listed syscall is denied by a verified active policy or request and completion effects are attributed.

surfaces.name: POSIX AIO and deferred native workers
arguments_and_variants: resolve which interfaces are present in the bound libc/dependency set
correlate request, worker/thread/process, underlying syscall, and completion
surfaces.resource: Deferred I/O requests executed by library-managed workers.
exclusions: There is no separate Linux syscall family named POSIX AIO; underlying worker syscalls are assigned to their canonical surfaces.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: Library-managed deferred work can obscure the causal link between workload request and native effect.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Bind the library interface set to the exact dependency/runtime identity and attribute worker operations and completions, or demonstrate a preventive control.

surfaces.name: Opaque and extensible kernel APIs
arguments_and_variants: No ioctl command is admitted for workload use; all commands, including FIONREAD, are proposed default-deny
bpf commands: no command admitted by this proposal; default-deny
perf_event_open: no operation admitted by this proposal; default-deny
userfaultfd: no operation admitted by this proposal; default-deny
surfaces.resource: Kernel interfaces whose command or operation semantics are selected through arguments.
exclusions: No command is excluded from the threat model solely because its semantics are opaque.
FIONREAD is an existing synthetic sensitivity/decoder case, not evidence that production policy permits it.

sensitivity_only_operations: ioctl(FIONREAD) on the previously used synthetic pipe fixture
proposed_policy.warning: FIONREAD is not admitted for workload use. The historical FIONREAD case calibrates telemetry only. All ioctl calls, plus bpf, perf_event_open, and userfaultfd, are proposed default-deny.

surfaces.threat_model_rationale: An opaque or extensible kernel API cannot be safely treated as covered from syscall-name visibility alone.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Either deny the complete syscall/API at an active verified boundary or enumerate command/operation, resource, arguments, and an enforceable allow rule with evidence.

surfaces.name: Namespace, mount, credentials, capabilities, and security-control mutation
arguments_and_variants: BOOTSTRAP/TRUSTED_INFRASTRUCTURE versus WORKLOAD phase
namespace type and target namespace identity
credential/capability before-and-after state
seccomp filter inheritance, stacking, and mutation attempt
mount API operation and target resource
surfaces.resource: Workload confinement state, privilege state, mount topology, and kernel security policy.
exclusions: Trusted launcher/bootstrap syscalls are not workload actions, but must remain phase-attributed and must not be omitted from trace-integrity requirements.
surfaces.threat_model_rationale: A potentially hostile workload must not widen its namespace, credentials, capabilities, or security policy beyond the trusted launch boundary.
surfaces.closure_criterion: Attribute phase and process; demonstrate prohibited workload transitions are denied by active policy or prove the resulting state and its security effect are observable and bounded.

sensor_requirements.name: Python sys.addaudithook telemetry
sensor_requirements.declared_limit: Python audit events are not a complete source of native syscall/effect telemetry; native_syscalls=false must remain explicit.
sensor_requirements.evidence_migration: Preserve the historical audit-harness-result.log reference under the ledger sensor requirement; do not retain sys.addaudithook as a workload mechanism.

python_native_traceability.scope: Static interface-family map only. A listed relationship is a candidate path, not evidence that a call site executes or that a specific syscall is emitted.
python_native_traceability.required_traceability_granularity: Each reachable call site in the exact workload snapshot -> Python API or dynamic entry point -> exact runtime/dependency implementation/version -> native extension/libc/direct syscall path -> syscall table row and surface/variant disposition.

static_inventory_basis.summary: 456 tracked test modules parsed; direct-call candidates 350 filesystem mutation, 126 filesystem read, 65 open, and 13 process. Categories overlap; the scanner found no imported-network-name patterns it recognizes, which is not evidence of absent network behavior.

python_native_traceability.method_limit: No complete AST call-site inventory or locked-dependency-to-extension map was available in the reviewed session documents. Dynamic dispatch, receiver types, transitive effects, ctypes/cffi, native extensions, callbacks, and transitive library behavior remain UNKNOWN. The static test inventory is a pre-screen, not a call graph or proof of runtime reachability. No current entry is a per-callsite, exact-version, syscall-row trace; STATIC_CANDIDATE is not OBSERVED, BLOCKED, or a completeness claim.

entries.limits: Exact syscall selection depends on CPython build, libc, flags, and runtime path.

entries.python_surface: os.open, os.openat where provided, os.access, os.stat, os.listdir, os.scandir, os.readlink
entries.native_or_library_layer: CPython os module and libc/syscall wrappers
entries.limits: Wrappers and fallback syscalls depend on Python, libc, kernel, and platform.

entries.python_surface: os.read, os.write, file-object read/write, buffered I/O
entries.limits: Buffering may coalesce calls; syscall events do not reveal payload when trace policy omits it.

entries.python_surface: os.unlink/remove, os.rename/replace, os.link, os.symlink, os.mkdir/rmdir, os.chmod/chown, os.truncate
entries.native_or_library_layer: CPython os module and libc/syscall wrappers
entries.limits: Exact variant depends on dir_fd support and the platform implementation.

entries.python_surface: mmap.mmap, mmap.flush, protection and mapping methods
entries.native_or_library_layer: CPython mmap extension and libc/syscall wrappers
entries.limits: The backing object, MAP_SHARED/MAP_PRIVATE and anonymous flags decide the canonical surface; CPU loads/stores are not syscall events.

entries.native_or_library_layer: CPython socket extension and libc/syscall wrappers
entries.limits: The socket domain and ancillary data depend on socket family/type and message control data.

entries.native_or_library_layer: CPython subprocess/posix modules and libc process-spawn implementation
entries.limits: Implementation strategy and descriptor actions are runtime/libc-dependent and require mapping to the exact pinned versions.

entries.native_or_library_layer: CPython threading runtime, multiprocessing bootstrap, libc and native extensions
entries.limits: Runtime implementation and worker-side effects are not fully statically mapped.

entries.python_surface: ctypes, cffi, C-extension modules, dynamically loaded native libraries and arbitrary callbacks
entries.native_or_library_layer: Arbitrary native code, direct syscalls, libc, or additional libraries
entries.limits: No finite syscall mapping follows from the Python API name alone; rely on the declared syscall-wide sensor/control boundary and fail closed on unclassified effects.

entries.python_surface: Python POSIX AIO bindings, if present in runtime/dependencies
entries.native_or_library_layer: libc POSIX AIO implementation and worker threads
entries.limits: The exact API availability and worker strategy must be bound to the runtime/dependency identity.

documentary_adjudication.disposition: Retain STATIC_CANDIDATE as a lead only and UNKNOWN where already assigned; do not interpret scanner candidate counts or no-match results as reachability/absence proof.
remaining_blockers: Exact workload snapshot callsites and dynamic entry points
Pinned CPython/libc/extension/dependency implementation versions for each reachable call
Native implementation to exact syscall row and argument partition
Dynamic dispatch, receiver types, transitive effects, ctypes/cffi, callbacks, and native extensions

sensitivity_controls.description: Deliberately injected regular FD verifies whether tracing attributes use of a capability whose pathname is absent inside the namespace.
sensitivity_controls.result_interpretation: OBSERVED sensitivity control only; does not show the normal launcher passed that capability.

sensitivity_controls.description: Deliberately injected external file FD calibrates tracing of file-backed MAP_SHARED creation/flush and independent read-back.
sensitivity_controls.result_interpretation: The mapping/flush is OBSERVED for this sensitivity case; it does not establish that the normal launcher passed the FD or that CPU stores are visible in the trace.

sensitivity_controls.description: Deliberately injected connected AF_UNIX FD verifies attribution of a send to an external peer.
sensitivity_controls.result_interpretation: OBSERVED sensitivity control only; does not show the normal launcher passed that capability.

sensitivity_controls.description: At sandbox entry, only explicitly declared descriptors are allowed; all undeclared descriptors must be closed or otherwise proven unavailable to the workload.
sensitivity_controls.existing_evidence_scope: Only a regular FD and the launcher path tested in the historical negative control; no generalization to other descriptor classes or later transfer paths.
